subject: Production streaming stalls causing client retry spiral
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@clearwavehealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: QA Team <qa@clearwavehealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T08:12:34-07:00
Subject: Production: intermittent streaming stalls triggering client retries

Evelyn —

We're seeing a production issue starting ~07:40 PDT where long-running chat completions intermittently stop emitting tokens for 10–30s and then resume. Our client-side logic treats the pause as a network failure and aggressively retries, creating a retry spiral that balloons 429/5xx errors across the account. This began after a normal traffic spike and is affecting ~12% of sessions.

Symptoms:
- Idle stalls mid-stream (~10s to 30s) where no tokens are received, connection stays open.
- Some clients then reconnect and re-send the same request, which leads to duplicated work and temporary 429 bursts.
- Overall p50 latency for completed responses is okay, but error rate and tail latency are high.

Attached: streaming_trace_20270509.log (snippet), client_stack_dump.txt

Can you confirm whether this looks like server-side idle disconnects, backend GC/queuing, or a routing fallback? We need an interim mitigation — our customers are seeing timeouts and several support tickets are escalating.

– Alex
Alex Mercer
Sr. Platform Engineer, ClearWave Health
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@clearwavehealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T08:35:02-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Production: intermittent streaming stalls triggering client retries

Following up from ClearWave (high-priority customer). They report mid-stream stalls that trigger client retries and spike 429/5xxs. Attaching their trace.

Quick ask: can infra/serving confirm whether there were any autoscale or node restarts, and whether prefix/KV cache interactions could explain a pause? Customer is asking for immediate mitigations to stop the retry spiral.

Immediate options I want us to consider:
- Short-term: add a server keepalive token every 5–10s for open streams to prevent client timeouts; advise customer to increase client idle timeout and apply exponential backoff on retries.
- Short-term: suppress duplicate requests server-side when the same client id + request id appear within a short window.
- Tactical: route ClearWave traffic to the next-capacity pool or a lower-capacity-constraint model variant while we investigate.

Marissa — flagging since this is escalating in Support. Sean/Rachel please triage.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@clearwavehealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T09:08:19-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: intermittent streaming stalls triggering client retries

Thanks Evelyn — I'm on it. Initial findings from the serving-side logs:

- No node restarts or container evictions in the ClearWave tenant pool during the window.
- We do see repeated keepalive absence events from a subset of connections followed by resumed token emission. The runtime marks these as idle but does not close the connection.
- In several traces the KV-prefix cache path had a small lock contention (median 120–250ms spikes) before the stall; that could allow a mid-stream pause if the generation worker is blocked waiting on a cache refill/lock.
- A small upstream proxy was returning 504 for in-flight connections when the worker delayed >20s, which then triggers client reconnect behavior.

Short-term mitigation I propose (low-risk, 1–2 hour changes):
1) Enable periodic keepalive pings on the server side for open streams (config flag: runtime.stream_keepalive=8s).
2) Temporarily extend customer connection window at the proxy to 45s for ClearWave to avoid 504s during these pauses.
3) Push a quick fix to make the prefix cache lock fast-fail: if a cache refill would block >300ms, return a soft-signal to continue generation without cache hit (config: cache.lock_fastfail=300ms).

Actions I will take now: enable keepalive and proxy window for ClearWave and monitor metrics. Can you confirm whether ClearWave can tolerate the extended proxy window? Alex, please confirm asap so we can flip the flags.

-Rachel
Staff SW Eng, Serving Runtime
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@clearwavehealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T09:22:10-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: intermittent streaming stalls triggering client retries

Thanks Rachel — we can tolerate an extended proxy window for the short term. We will also patch our client to add a conservative 30s idle timeout + exponential backoff for retries, and to include a request-id header to help dedupe.

Two follow-ups from our side:
- I've uploaded fuller traces to the Drive link you gave and included a short video of client behavior.
- We are concerned about the duplicate billing/compute for repeated streams — any throttling or dedupe on your end would be appreciated.

Appreciate the rapid response.

— Alex
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@clearwavehealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-10T15:46:21-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: intermittent streaming stalls triggering client retries

Update and next steps for executive/ops tracker:

- Rachel enabled runtime.stream_keepalive=8s and cache.lock_fastfail=300ms at 09:12 PDT on 2027-05-09. Proxy window for ClearWave extended to 45s at the same time. We observed immediate drop in customer-side retry re-submits and a 60% reduction in 429s for ClearWave over the next 90 minutes.
- Engineering will run a follow-up: a controlled load test with synthetic long streams to reproduce the cache lock path under pressure (INF-4521).
- Product/Finance: discuss an interim credit for duplicated runs billed during the spike. Draft proposal: 20% credit for the affected billing window, pending final RCA.

I'll open a short post-incident summary and assign owners:
- Root cause investigation: Rachel Kim (serving runtime)
- Customer communication & credits: Evelyn Hart (account) + Sean Gallagher (support)
- Long-term mitigation (runtime change): Platform team to evaluate switching to an optimistic cache refill + background refresh pattern.

Thanks team — please add any other items to INF-4521. I'll be briefed in tomorrow's ops sync at 10:00 PDT.

-Marissa
Director, Customer Success
